summary.text: Patrick McMath is a Republican member of the Louisiana Senate, representing District 11 (St. Tammany Parish), and was elected in 2019, according to the official Senate member page. He chairs the Senate Health and Welfare Committee.

paragraphs.text: McMath earned a B.A. in Political Science from Louisiana State University and a J.D. from Loyola University New Orleans College of Law, according to his Senate biography.
Before entering politics he served as an assistant district attorney in Louisiana's 22nd Judicial District Court.
The biography says he is involved with the St. Tammany Chamber of Commerce, the Boys and Girls Club of Covington, the Kelly Gibson Foundation and the Child Advocacy Center-Hope House.
It describes a focus on infrastructure improvements, tax reform, public safety and state investment in community service organizations, and says he is married to Jayne and has four children.

The page lists committee assignments including Health and Welfare (chair), Judiciary B, Transportation, Highways and Public Works, the Legislative Audit Advisory Council and the Senate Select Committee on Women and Children, and caucus affiliations including the Louisiana Republican Legislative Delegation and the Northshore Delegation.
